content.text: can you explain the conceptual difference between affix and proc node?

Conceptually:

- An affix is authored item content: “Soul Drain,” “Flaming,” “Guarded.” It describes the modifier attached to an item and may be passive or reactive.
- A proc node is runtime execution topology: a concrete node with triggers, gates, priorities, and effects that the rules engine evaluates.

So the relationship is roughly:

```text
authored affix
  → compiled into
runtime proc node
  → evaluated by combat
```

The screenshot exposed an architecture leak: the UI was displaying the runtime implementation (“Proc Nodes”) instead of the player-facing mechanic.

The newer approach keeps the proc topology hidden and gives the authored mechanic an explicit display description, such as:

```text
Equip: On hit, 18% chance to heal for half the damage dealt.
```

Proc packages already followed that model. Classical affixes did not, which is why Leech Blade slipped through. The migration path is to add authored display metadata to affix definitions, use it to render Equip mechanics, and suppress the corresponding runtime proc nodes while leaving combat behavior unchanged.

Good progress: the conceptual migration is now generalized beyond Leech Blade. I’ve moved the display metadata into the classical affix definitions themselves, so every item using an affix can get a player-facing Equip line and have its implementation proc nodes hidden consistently. I’m running the broader display/proc checks now and will report any wording or coverage issues.
